critical_steps: Every array literally displayed in Note 3.2 is an outer product in the two-by-two scalar model and has determinant zero.
Two allowed rank-one diagonal arrays sum to the identity matrix, which is not of the displayed form.
The full coefficient space is the l2 direct sum over the product index set.
The map U from the tensor product of one-factor coefficient spaces to the product-index direct sum is isometric on simple tensors and has dense range, hence is unitary.
The source synthesis computation becomes the bounded-operator identity T_product U = T_Lambda tensor T_Gamma.
integrity.proof_basis: A two-by-two scalar rank argument and a direct construction of the canonical unitary between the tensor product of coefficient direct sums and the direct sum over the product index set.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made about the authors' unstated intended interpretation beyond the literal displayed definition.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects the coefficient-space definition and synthesis-operator identification; it does not refute the tensor-product frame-operator identity after domains are repaired.

If the printed separable-array notation was intended informally as the full direct sum, the defect is definitional rather than an intended restriction, but the canonical unitary is still needed for the synthesis-operator equality.
No higher-fold tensor-product generalization is asserted beyond the analogous standard unitary identification.
title: The tensor-product \(g\)-fusion synthesis domain is not a vector space
